episodes.211485: A small line segment of strong thunderstorms developed during the late evening hours. The storms produced gusty winds and heavy downpours which knocked down trees at a few locations in Morgan County.
episodes.211538: Waves of thunderstorms passed through Central Alabama from April 28 into April 29, affecting predominantly northwestern Central Alabama. A few instances of hail and wind damage occurred from the morning to the evening of April 28 across Marion, Winston, and Lamar counties, with a couple more areas of wind damage reported in Fayette and Walker counties just after midnight. The next evening, a localized area of tree damage occurred in Irondale in Jefferson County, which included a couple trees falling onto homes.
episodes.211571: A well-defined shortwave embedded within a zonal flow along with mid-level lapse rates around 7 C/km and mid-level flow around 40 knots supported strong thunderstorms capable of producing marginally severe hail.
episodes.211603: During the early morning hours on April 30th a line of thunderstorms moved through the Central Savannah River Area producing an isolated incident of wind damage in the vicinity of the Savannah River Site where a 200ft tower measured a wind gust of 78 mph. The atmosphere was weakly unstable with SBCAPE values approaching 1000 J/kg and 0-6km shear around 40 knots. PWAT values were around 1.3 inches.
episodes.211632: A traveler driving on I-25 observed a large and intense dust devil looking east towards the Sandia Mountains during the early afternoon hours of April 30th. Another large and intense dust devil was observed from a traveler driving in Cochiti Pueblo. The size and nature of the dust devils based on the videos taken by the travelers resulted in high interest from local and national media outlets.
episodes.211641: An approaching cold front, supported by an upper-level shortwave trough, triggered widely scattered thunderstorms. Decreasing cloud cover during late afternoon allowed instability to increase, with CAPE values in Blacksburg, VA reaching as high as 3,000 J/Kg per the 30/00z upper air sounding. Lapse rates were observed near 7 C/km, while 0-1km shear was observed at around 40 knots. Storms developed along the Blue Ridge and pushed east into the Piedmont, increasing in intensity across the southern Piedmont. Storms then congealed into a broken line that tracked southeast. Although no hail was reported, there were several reports of trees blown down by thunderstorm winds.
episodes.211642: An approaching cold front, supported by an upper-level shortwave trough, triggered widely scattered thunderstorms. Decreasing cloud cover during late afternoon allowed instability to increase, with CAPE values in Blacksburg, VA reaching as high as 3,000 J/Kg per the 30/00z upper air sounding. Lapse rates were observed near 7 C/km, while 0-1km shear was observed at around 40 knots. Storms developed along the Blue Ridge and pushed east into the Piedmont, increasing in intensity across the southern Piedmont. Storms then congealed into a broken line that tracked southeast. Although no hail was reported, there were several reports of trees blown down by thunderstorm winds.
episodes.211972: A shortwave trough, slow moving cold front, and continued presence of a dryline resulted in additional severe thunderstorm development on April 28 and 29. Large hail was the primary severe weather occurrence. Destructive hail damaged several locations in North and Central Texas with hail sizes ranging up to 3.5-4 inch hail in Johnson County. On April 28th 4 tornadoes occurred including an EF-3 tornado in Mineral Wells.
episodes.212043: A storm produced a strong wind gust over Winyah Bay.
episodes.212044: A home was damaged by lightning in Socastee, SC.
episodes.212150: A lone hail storm developed over portions of Madison county.
episodes.212686: Behind the northward retreat of a warm front, a cluster of showers moved along and just ahead of a cold front from Virginia into northwest North Carolina during the evening hours. These showers deepened and led to growing clusters of storms, along with one sustained supercell that brought a swath of large hail (0.75 to 1.25) and sporadic power outages and downed trees to the northern Piedmont and northern Coastal Plain during the late evening hours.
episodes.212708: Well above normal April rainfall upstream along the Ohio River from East Central Missouri and Central Illinois to Iowa/Wisconsin resulted in river levels on the Mississippi River rising into minor flood at Chester and Cape Girardeau to end the month, with minor flooding continuing into May. Impacts were limited to bottomland agricultural areas.
episodes.212745: On the afternoon of April 30th, locally induced showers with isolated thunderstorms developed over portions of the interior and north-central PR and steered by southeasterly winds towards the western half. This resulted in urban and small stream flooding, as well as isolated flash flooding, over sectors of interior to western PR including Hormigueros through the evening hours.
episodes.212932: A broad area of mostly elevated strong to severe thunderstorms developed and shifted southward across Southeast Oklahoma into the Ark-La-Tex along an advancing cold front throughout the day on April 29th. Modest low-level warm air advection atop a slightly stable, near-surface layer managed to sustain the convection within a more moderately unstable and strongly sheared environment aloft. As a result, the environment remained favorable for embedded supercell structures capable of large hail. Given the relatively closer proximity of the southernmost storms to the surface front, the threat for severe wind gusts also continued southeast toward the boundary. As a result, numerous reports of large hail were recorded across parts of East Texas along with an isolated report of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.213008: Thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a stationary front, and some of these storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.213108: Thunderstorms developed along a slow-moving cold front. Some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.213203: A cold front slowly moved south into the region on April 29th while a warm, moist, and unstable airmass was in place across southwest Mississippi. Thunderstorms developed along and ahead of the front during the afternoon hours, then became increasingly influenced by storm outflow as they moved south faster than the front itself. The strongest storms produced a mix of large hail and damaging wind across portions of southwest Mississippi.
episodes.213205: A cold front sagged southward into the region on April 30th, becoming positioned near the Interstate 10 and 12 corridors by the afternoon. A moist and unstable airmass remained in place from the previous day while a passing upper level disturbance helped showers and thunderstorms redevelop and intensify during the late afternoon. The strongest storms produced heavy rainfall over portions of the Baton Rouge metro area in a short period of time. The combination of slow-moving storms, locally heavy downpours, and urban drainage impacts led to flash flooding in parts of the metro area.
episodes.214397: Well above normal April rainfall upstream along the Ohio River from East Central Missouri and Central Illinois to Iowa/Wisconsin resulted in river levels on the Mississippi River rising into minor flood at Cape Girardeau to end the month, with minor flooding continuing into May. Impacts were limited to bottomland agricultural areas.
